Commentary.Commentary: We are all set for England's reply! The umpires are back out in the middle and so are the players of India. It will be Ben Duckett and Zak Crawley to open the innings for England. Jasprit Bumrah has the new ball in hand and is raring to go. Let's play...
... THIRD INNINGS ...

India have a massive lead of 190 runs but they will be a tad disappointed to have added just 15 runs on Day 3. Both Ravindra Jadeja and Axar Patel were a bit passive against the likes of Mark Wood and Joe Root and the runs only flowed in the one over that Jack Leach bowled. Jadeja kept on just blocking and missed one that got him out LBW and then it was all over within a span of five minutes. However, that stand between Jadeja and Axar has given India a good chance of bundling out the opposition and they have a real shot of an innings victory here. A big innings in the context of the match is coming up and all eyes will be on the English openers. Join us in a few minutes as England's second innings is up next.

Right then, a quick turnaround for England in the first hour or so on Day 3 and they will be fairly relieved to have not conceded many runs either. Joe Root has been their best bowler and got a couple of quick wickets to give his side the much-needed breather and ended with 4 wickets overall. Rehan Ahmed then came in and got the final wicket to keep India's lead under the 200-run mark. Overall, it was a sedate display with the ball but they have done well here to give themselves half a chance of making a comeback in the game.

OUT! TIMBER! It's all over for India as they are bowled out for 436! A short ball outside the line of the off stump, gets it to turn back sharp into the stumps. Axar Patel stays back and looks to cut it hard but the lack of bounce on the ball beats his bat and rushes onto the middle stump. Axar Patel goes for a well-made 44. India conclude their first innings with a lead of 190.

Commentary.Commentary: We are all set! The Umpires and the players are out in the field and ready to start the Day 3. Ravindra Jadeja and Axar Patel are the overnight batters for India. Mark Wood to start the attack for England on Day 3. Let's Play!
... DAY 3, FIRST SESSION ...

England haven't been able to make inroads with the ball and a lot will depend on their top order when they eventually do come out to bat but it is going to be a really difficult ask for them. Stay tuned as the start of Day 3 isn't far away.
India have a huge first innings lead and aren't quite done yet with the bat and with the spin attack they have, they will be looking to make the second English innings the last one of the game.

Hello and a warm welcome to Day 3 of the first Test match between India and England at the Rajiv Gandhi International Stadium in Hyderabad. The hosts have enjoyed an amazing couple of days and are well ahead in the game. England will need to conjure up a special performance with the bat to salvage something here.
... DAY 3, SESSION 1...

Right then, India already lead by 175 runs which is massive and with still some gas left in the tank, it could get really amazing for them. As for England, they have been dealt a big blow in the very first innings of the very first Test match on this long red-ball tour and will have to pull off an amazing heist to take the game into a fourth innings. Day 3 is generally the moving day and we are well poised to see plenty of action one way or another. Day 3 will begin on Saturday at 9.30 am IST (4 am GMT) but you can join us a lot sooner for the build-up. Cheers!

KL Rahul is down for a quick chat and says that the hundred in South Africa has given him a lot of confidence. He was just looking to enjoy his batting and is happy with where the team stands. He also adds that the wickets are very different from that in South Africa but that is the challenge, he has to adapt to the conditions and play accordingly. He finally talks about his mindset of being a middle-order batter and says that it helps him prepare better as to the plans of the bowler. Ends by saying that they are looking to bat as long as possible as there are still 3 days to come in this Test match.

England have been made to toil long and hard in the field and at the end of it all, they look to be heading toward a heavy defeat with the style of batting they have adapted to, there is still that glimmer of hope but it is quite slim. The bowling from all bowlers was erratic but Jack Leach did provide a bit of control whenever he bowled and Joe Root looked the most likely to pick up a wicket. Root, who will have to play a big role in the next innings with the bat had to do a fair bit with the ball and in the field as well which will surely take its toll on him. The two young spinners in the form of Rehan Ahmed and Tom Hartley just haven't been able to match their counterparts and have received a lot of stick throughout the day. England need to be on it early on Day 3 if they are to make any impact in the second innings.

SESSION SUMMARY - 34 overs, 112 runs and 2 wickets. End of a pretty engrossing day of Test cricket that has seen India take complete control of the game and with the lead being stretched to 175 runs, they will have an eye on the 200-run mark and with two batters who have both spent time on the crease, it looks like a mere formality. In all three sessions, India lost a couple of wickets but managed to build partnerships right throughout, never allowing the opposition to make a comeback in the game. Ravindra Jadeja has played a fabulous unbeaten knock of 81 runs after a couple of 80s from Yashasvi Jaiswal and KL Rahul and has been well-supported by the likes of KS Bharat who scored 41 before getting out and now Axar Patel who is unbeaten on 35.

FOUR! He goes again, what a way to finish a day! Slogs it away over mid-wicket for a one-bounce boundary. Fuller again by Tom Hartley outside the off stump line and Axar Patel slogs one again this time in front of deep mid-wicket and the ball bounces just inside the boundary line. India finish Day 2 on 421/7.

Commentary.Commentary: We are back for the post-Lunch session on Day 2! The umpires are back out in the middle and so are the English players. KL Rahul and Shreyas Iyer are all set to resume their stay at the crease as well. It will be Rehan Ahmed to begin proceedings with the ball after the break.
... DAY 2, SESSION 2 ...

England might have been frustrated last evening with the runs flowing but they will be even more frustrated this morning. Joe Root finally got the ball and in the very first over of the Day, got rid of the dangerman Yashasvi Jaiswal. After that though, Ben Stokes employed the same tactics from Day 1 by bowling Tom Hartley for a long spell and that didn't work out. They created a bit of early pressure but bowled way too many bad balls and Root wasn't used much after his first spell of four overs. Mark Wood bowled a fiery spell in the middle but the short deliveries were put away by KL Rahul and then finally Tom Hartley got one wicket. At the moment though, England are staring at a big first-innings deficit and will have to turn things around very quickly if they are to stay in the game. Join us at 12.10 pm IST (6.40 am GMT) for the post-Lunch session.

SESSION SUMMARY - 27 overs, 103 runs and 2 wickets. The first session of Day 2 and it was once again dominated by India and even though they lost a couple of wickets, the runs kept on flowing and they are now just 24 runs away from England's first innings total with 7 wickets in hand. The man on song from last evening, Yashasvi Jaiswal perished in the very first over of the day after hitting a boundary but then KL Rahul walked in at number 4 for the first time in Tests and he didn't miss a beat from the very off. Rahul did nick one very early on but that was it and he scored freely against the spinners. Shubman Gill couldn't turn his shaky start from last evening into a positive one and held out mid-way through the session. Shreyas Iyer looked tentative at the start but hit his way out of trouble and now the set pair of Rahul and Iyer looks set to pile on the misery on the visitors.
